status: AMENDED 8 October 2026 (cloud week 42) from the lab's target of the same day. The photographs P1 and P2 decide every point where they disagree with a book (Jafar's ruling); every element of both photographs was gone through again, edges and furniture included. self_check below is written by self_check.py.
axes: x across the opening (left to right seen from outside), z up, y depth into the wall with the outside at -y. Origin: the left brick reveal edge (x=0), the top of the stone threshold under the leaf (z=0), the outside face of the brick wall (y=0). Ground is below z=0 (T1 -258, F1 -70). glb pivot: base centre on the ground, x = the opening's centre (T1 441, F1 472), y = 0, z = ground.

knob.note: No knob or pull in P1.

P1 (fresh, 2012): a glossy fresh coat, brush marks running with the grain (fine lines down the stiles and muntin)
grime on the weatherboard's and the band's top nosings, the dark crease under the band
a stained, brown-gold threshold front and a worn pale nosing on the step
the frame's foot dirty with splash
a dark shadow line under the transom nose and under the band
P2 (old, 2024 photograph of an unrestore: crazed ('alligator') paint over the whole leaf, cells 2-4 mm, dark in the cracks
bare pale patches and chipped paint on the lower right panel's moulding and on the bottom rail
dirt packed in the mouldings' angles, the bottom rail wet-grimed and flaking
the frame's paint peeling in sheets down to a darker undercoat, hairline cracks along the stop
plugged and abandoned holes (an old keyhole, screw holes), stickers and tape marks (leave out)
a worn bare-wood threshold with flaked paint; cracked paving slab in front
wear.1990 rule for the kit: unrestored, not heritage-fresh: crazing and chips on arrises and mouldings' lower lips, paint 15% duller, grime in the mouldings' angles and on every upward face, wet-darkened and flaking paint on the bottom rail, the weatherboard, the frame's foot and the threshold, brass dull with bright touched edges. Cables, junction boxes, stickers and the wall lantern in the photographs are not part of the kit.

edges._note: Every edge the photographs show, with its treatment. 'eased' means a 1 mm paint-rounded arris, not a modelled round.
edges.jamb, head and transom ends: square; eased 1 mm; NO ovolo, NO bead on the outer arris, NO tube-like rounding (P1, P2); the face is one flat plane
edges.stop's inner edge: T1: square (one dark 1 px line in P1); F1: a planted quarter-round bead 5 wide x 2.5 proud on each jamb (P2's light line)
edges.frame feet: square-cut, standing on the threshold at z 0, both alike; no step, plinth or block; the brick plinth hides them in T1
edges.leaf's outer edges: square, eased 1.5 mm; 1.6 mm shadow gap to the rebate wall all round; the leaf's bottom edge is square, 10 mm above the threshold
edges.bolection mouldings: a crease where the moulding's outer edge meets the framing (0.0 on the profile), a rounded nose of about 3.5 mm radius at d 1.4-5.5, a short fillet, a convex bead falling into a cove that ends on the panel field; mitred at the corners with tight, closed mitres
edges.lock-rail band: square underside (the crisp shadow line), lower lip with a 3 mm round, a cove, a bead, a groove, a rounded top nosing of about 13 mm radius rolling back to the rail
edges.weatherboard: flat underside flush with the leaf's bottom, a convex belly, a hollow near its top, a rounded top nose of about 13 mm radius rolling back onto the door
edges.transom: a lip bead of 2.6 mm radius at its underside, a cove, a vertical face, a weathered slope; its ends square against the jamb faces
edges.glazing bead: quarter-round 10 x 8 with a 1.5 mm flat at its foot, mitred on all four sides
edges.threshold stone: rounded top nose, radius 18; its ends square where they enter the brick; its underside square, overhanging the riser by 18 (the shadow gap)
edges.step tread: bullnose, radius 30, along its front; plan corners radius 40; the top falls 6.6 mm to the front
edges.arch bricks: bricks on end, square arrises, 8 mm joints, the face joints raked back 4 mm (dark lines); the soffit (underside) seen as dark brick ends
edges.letter plate: outer corners square with a 2 mm round; the rim's outer edge chamfered 45 degrees from 6 mm down to the backplate; the flap hinged along its top edge with a 2 mm shadow gap
edges.cylinder lock: collar T1 plain with a bevelled edge; F1 knurled with 12 serrations; flush bore of 1.5 to 2 mm collar relief

joints_and_seams.stile-to-rail joints: paint-bridged hairlines 0.4 mm wide at every rail/stile meeting on the face, dark in the 1990 wear mask (P2 shows them as thin cracks)
joints_and_seams.mitres of the mouldings: closed; a dark hairline only where the paint has cracked (wear mask), never a 0.3 mm-plus gap (the lab's review 1, fault 7)
joints_and_seams.leaf to frame: 1.6 mm shadow gap on the three sides and the head (P1, P2 dark lines); the bottom gap 10 mm to the threshold
joints_and_seams.frame to brick: a 3 mm dark joint between the jamb and the reveal (P1); in F1 a groove of 5-7 mm between the jamb strip and the pilaster's return (P2)
joints_and_seams.band and weatherboard ends: 2 mm short of the stop faces, a dark line
joints_and_seams.transom to jambs: the transom's front member butts on the jamb faces; a hairline each side
joints_and_seams.glass to bead: a light putty-and-bead line 1-2 px wide (P1)

fixings.letter plate: T1: none seen at 5 mm a pixel; F1: four slotted screws 4 mm Dia at the rim's corners (P2)
fixings.cylinder lock: no screws seen; a flush collar
fixings.mouldings: slot-screwed and pinned from behind (Ellis p.92): nothing on the face
fixings.frame: plugs, wedges and horns in the wall (Ellis p.111-112): hidden
fixings.house numbers: two screws or pins each, not seen

drips_and_throats.weatherboard: the drip on the door's foot: it throws rain off the bottom rail; its hollow is a throat
drips_and_throats.transom: the weathered slope sheds rain from the glass's foot to the front; the nose's underside is a drip over the leaf's head
drips_and_throats.threshold: the 18 mm overhang of its nose over the riser makes the shadow gap (a throat)
drips_and_throats.band: its flat underside throws a crisp shadow; no throat
drips_and_throats.head: none seen; the arch's soffit overhangs the frame's head by 0 (flush)

terrace_four_panel.description: T1: the four-panel front door of the terraces: P1's door in its brick opening with a segmental buff-brick arch, buff quoins, a stone threshold and a deep stone step. Colours: door_colours (weights), frame_colours. Count: the scene's.

flat_door_over_shop.description: F1: the side door to a flat over a shop: the same four-panel door at the street's 0.838 x 1.981, a 102 mm moulded and weathered transom projecting 22 mm over the head, P2's furniture (turned centre knob, cylinder lock and plugged keyhole, a letter plate), no band, no weatherboard, a worn timber threshold at the pavement, no step, no brick arch (the shopfront holds the head). Colours: door_colours without 'red' (weights renormalised), frame white or cream.

could_not_settle: No dated 1975 to 2000 photograph of a four-panel door of the street's kind was reachable: P1 is dated 6 May 2012 (fresh paint, door possibly renewed), P2 is 3 February 2024 (an unrestored six-panel door). Egress refused Geograph, Wikimedia Commons, archive.org and the wider web.
The bolection moulding's width (34 +-8 on P1, 43 on P2) and the transom's, band's and weatherboard's projections (judged from shadow lengths) are not measurable at 480 px.
The step's depth (312) and thickness (110) and the ground level at the foot: perspective hides them; +-80 mm.
The jamb's visible width on the flat door: the bay's 0.944 gives 73 mm; P2 shows a 49 mm strip (and a groove) between the leaf and the shop's pilaster. If the bay can give 47 mm, the jamb shows 50.
Whether the leaf is 1948 or 1926 high (1%): the left edge leans 2.6 px over 210 rows in P1.
The lock rail band's and the weatherboard's exact sections: the photograph gives highlights and shadows, not outlines; the profiles are drawn to reproduce them, not measured.
How the transom's nose ends at the jambs (square end, return or mitre): P2 shows it rolling over the stop edge; a square end is specified.
Hinge details (inside, not seen); the plinth and dog-tooth course of P1's wall (the wall's own); the colour of an actual Hook door in 1990 (no source).
